problem.title: Most digital products fail on strategy, not code.

items.title: Misaligned goals
items.body: Business, operations and technology each optimise for a different result.

items.title: Hiring too early
items.body: A full-time product leader is hired before the problem is defined.

items.title: Pilots that stall
items.body: A good demo, but no adoption plan and no owner after launch.

services.title: Six services, one senior team
services.lead: Each service ends with a decision made or a system in use, not a slide deck.

items.title: 0→1 product discovery
items.body: Strategy, MVP scope, business case and build-or-buy evaluation, so the first release answers the right question.

items.title: Delivery and rollout
items.body: Agile delivery, UAT, release readiness and change management until people actually use the product.

items.title: Process digitalization
items.body: Paper, spreadsheets and legacy tools replaced by systems that operations teams choose to use.

items.title: Data and AI readiness
items.body: KPI definitions, data governance and semantic models, so AI works on numbers the business trusts.

items.title: Fractional product leadership
items.body: A senior product lead embedded in your team, without a full-time hire.

items.title: Vendor evaluation
items.body: Fit, cost, scalability, integration effort and security assessed before a contract is signed.

approach.title: Four steps from question to adopted product

steps.title: Discover
steps.body: Map workflows and decision points. Find the real problem.

steps.title: Define
steps.body: Agree scope, KPIs and trade-offs before anything is built.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.body: Ship in small slices, each with a named owner.

steps.title: Adopt
steps.body: Train, measure and iterate until the numbers move.

callout.title: Need more than three people? Partners are screened before they join.
callout.body: Engineering and design partners are assessed on fit, cost, scalability and security by the people who will run your project.
